introduction.text: The Mausoleo di Menenio Agrippa is a Roman mausoleum located on Via Nomentana near the Ponte Nomentano, notable for its 1st–2nd century AD construction and its association with the historical figure Menenio Agrippa.

history.description: Menenio Agrippa, who lived in the 1st century BC, is traditionally associated with the mausoleum, although he lived six centuries before its construction.
The mausoleum itself dates to the 1st–2nd century AD.
In the 16th–17th centuries, the mausoleum was depicted with a medieval tower, a feature that no longer exists.
Pillars of reinforcement were added to the structure on the Via Nomentana side.
A portion of the wall was relocated to the opposite side of the street.
Access to the mausoleum was blocked after its abandonment.

design.description: The mausoleum has a circular plan on a parallelepiped base, built with opus cementicium (mortar and yellow tuff). It features a vaulted funerary chamber made from amphora fragments, four niches, and windows.
